name: Warren Magic
laws: Each warren is a metaphysical realm with its own laws
Mages draw power by opening a warren
Warrens can be traveled physically by those with sufficient affinity
Some warrens are broken, corrupted, or lost
costs: Warren corruption can follow the mage out (e.g., Chaos warren)
Ascendancy binds the mage to their warren's logic
limits: Cannot open a warren one has no affinity for
Some warrens require consent from a god/House
examples: The corruption of Chaos throughout the Book of the Fallen

name: Convergence as Narrative Principle
laws: Independent threads grow from independent pressure
Each thread has its own timeline and its own logic
Convergence is necessity at the level of each character's arc, not coincidence at the author's level
The meeting-point is the place where all pressures peak simultaneously
costs: Reader may feel untethered for entire acts
Resolution must honor all threads, not just the foreground
limits: Cannot fake convergence; threads must genuinely intersect by necessity
Cannot use deus ex machina; the collapse must be foreseeable in retrospect
examples: The final battles of The Crippled God
